meta.task: prior_hunt_0 - arXiv and venue sweep 2025 through 2026-07 for papers we do not have
meta.agent_note: This file is the deliverable. The structured-output receipt carries only counts, this path and highlights.
meta.rule: Every factual claim below carries (a) an exact PDF path or a resolved DOI, (b) which version, (c) the quoted sentence. Anything missing one of the three is marked UNVERIFIED.
search_surfaces: Semantic Scholar citation graph of arXiv:2303.11103 (276 citers) and arXiv:2203.11854 (508 citers)
meta.known_blind_spot: arXiv all: search covers title/abstract/comments/journal-ref, NOT full text. Papers that use Sionna without saying so in the abstract are invisible to it; the Semantic Scholar citation sweep partly compensates.

h8_assessment.statement_under_test: Zero PUBLISHED papers compute a validated scattering signature from a drone mesh in a Sionna-class engine.
h8_assessment.verdict: SURVIVES, but only in its "validated" form. The looser readings are now refuted.
what_this_sweep_refuted: REFUTED: "no published paper puts a drone mesh into Sionna." Clutter-Aware ISAC (Proceedings of the IEEE) does exactly that - "The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3D mesh objects imported into Sionna."

REFUTED: "no published paper derives a drone signature from a mesh." AirGuard (IEEE JSAC 44:835-848, 2026) derives cmD and HRRP from a drone .obj mesh - though by point-cloud geometry, with zero electromagnetics.
NARROWED: "the SBR+PO-on-a-graphics-renderer architecture is ours." arXiv:2511.07586 does SBR + PO on Mitsuba and verifies it on aircraft (preprint).
h8_assessment.what_survives: Across everything opened in this sweep, no PUBLISHED paper computes a drone-mesh scattering signature with an electromagnetic surface integral in a Sionna-class engine AND validates the resulting level against measurement. The two published mesh-based drone papers both avoid the amplitude question: Clutter-Aware ISAC uses stock materials for relative clutter maps; AirGuard uses isotropic scattering points for a classification score.
h8_assessment.recommended_wording: Published work has put drone meshes into Sionna (Proc. IEEE) and derived drone signatures from meshes (IEEE JSAC), but neither computes an electromagnetic surface integral nor validates an absolute scattering level; the one Mitsuba-based SBR+PO implementation that does validate levels is a preprint and targets aircraft, not drones.
h8_assessment.residual_risk: This remains a negative claim of the E1 shape. It is now based on 28 newly opened PDFs plus the existing archive, but arXiv metadata search does not index full text, so a paper that uses Sionna without saying so in its abstract can still be missed.

settlements.ledger_question: Clutter-Aware ISAC: does it use Sionna at all? And is arXiv:2602.10537 a different document from the Proc. IEEE PDF the census read?
settlements.verdict: SETTLED - the two are the SAME work, and the "no Sionna" claim is REFUTED in BOTH.

evidence.fact: arXiv:2602.10537v2 is the same paper as the archived Proc. IEEE PDF.
evidence.support: arXiv comment field of v2: "36 pages, 12 figures. Accepted by Proceedings of the IEEE". Machine keyword census over both PDFs is near-identical (sionna 13 vs 13, ray-tracing 7 vs 7, mesh 2 vs 2, Blender 1 vs 1, CAD 1 vs 1, cfar 4 vs 4, false_alarm 3 vs 3).

evidence.fact: The paper DOES use Sionna, ray tracing and meshes.
evidence.verbatim_quote: These meshes are obtained by simplifying publicly available 3D models in Blender and exporting them in Sionna’s XML format, which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment.
evidence.version: arXiv v2 (also present in the Proc. IEEE PDF)

evidence.fact: UAVs specifically are meshes in Sionna.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3D mesh objects imported into Sionna.

evidence.fact: Concrete engine setting recorded by the paper.
evidence.verbatim_quote: The maximum interaction depth for Sionna is set to three, so each ray undergoes at most three interactions with scene objects.

settlements.consequence: The contradiction was NOT caused by two different documents. One of our own files carries a straightforwardly false negative claim ("no Sionna, no ray tracing, no mesh, target as an abstract complex coefficient"). The other file (Sionna appears 12-13 times, Blender-simplified meshes, Sionna XML) is correct, and the phrase "Sionna’s XML format" is verbatim.
settlements.error_pattern: E1 (a negative claim asserting what the paper does not contain, when it does)

settlements.ledger_question: Clutter-Aware ISAC CFAR vocabulary: prose says Pd/Pfa/ROC zero and ECA/CLEAN/CAF zero; machine count says cfar=4, false_alarm=3.
settlements.verdict: SETTLED - the MACHINE COUNT is right and the prose is PARTLY WRONG.

evidence.fact: CFAR appears 4 times and "false alarm" 3 times in BOTH versions.
evidence.verbatim_quote: To maintain a prescribed false-alarm probability, range-Doppler constant false-alarm rate (CFAR) detectors estimate the local interference power from neighboring training cells around the cell under test and adapt the threshold accordingly.

evidence.fact: ROC, ECA, CLEAN, CAF and "detection probability" DO each appear zero times - those parts of our prose are correct.
evidence.support: regex census over the full extracted text of both PDFs: roc=0, eca=0, clean=0, caf=0, pd_detection_prob=0.

settlements.consequence: Restate as a claim about EXECUTED EVALUATION, not vocabulary: the paper discusses CFAR as background (one of its four mentions is "Representative CFAR variants and comparative studies can be found in [49]") but reports no ROC, no Pd/Pfa curve, and no ECA/CLEAN/CAF processing.

settlements.ledger_question: Yuan (EuCAP 2025): monostatic 3D UAV RCS, slopes 0.315/0.231/0.175 dB/GHz at theta=90/0/180.
settlements.verdict: A SECOND E2 HAZARD FOUND - there are TWO different Yuan papers and our files may be blending them.

evidence.fact: Document A (the one in our archive, 5 pages): "On Experimental Analysis of Mono-Static 3D UAV RCS for ISAC Channel Modeling", authors Zhiqiang Yuan, Le Yu, Chunhui Li, Wei Fan (FOUR authors), all National Mobile Communications Research Laboratory, Southeast University, Nanjing. Measures 1.8-18.2 GHz, azimuth -90 to +90 deg, at THREE UAV elevation sides {90, 0, 180} deg.
evidence.verbatim_quote: we conduct mono-static UAV RCS measurements in an anechoic chamber, recording RCS covering frequency band of 1.8 ~18.2 GHz and azimuth angles of -90 deg ~90 deg (given the symmetry of the UAV) at three UAV elevation sides {90 deg, 0 deg, 180 deg}
evidence.caveat: Page 1 of this PDF carries NO venue stamp. "EuCAP 2025" is therefore UNVERIFIED from the PDF itself.

evidence.fact: Document B (journal, NOT in our archive): "Experimental Analysis and Modeling of Monostatic AAV RCS for ISAC Channels", IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters, vol.24, pp.222-226, Jan 2025, DOI 10.1109/lawp.2024.3492502, SIX authors: Yuan Zhiqiang, Yu Le, Wang Zhiqin, Li Chunhui, Dallmann Thomas, Fan Wei. Says AAV not UAV; abstract contains NO "3D" and NO three-elevation-sides sentence.
evidence.support: Crossref bibliographic query + 6G Flagship publication page (verbatim abstract retrieved)

settlements.consequence: ⭐ The theta = 90/0/180 deg slopes can only come from Document A (the 3D one). Attributing them to the AWPL letter would be a fresh E3-shaped error. Also: the two documents differ in author count (4 vs 6) and in the UAV/AAV wording.
settlements.open: The "EuCAP 2025" venue for Document A remains UNVERIFIED - no venue string on its first page and no Crossref hit under that title.

settlements.verdict: VENUE AND PAGES CONFIRMED EXACTLY; band is WIDER than sometimes assumed; a companion preprint exists with a DIFFERENT band.

evidence.support: Crossref bibliographic query; the archived PDF header also reads "IEEE WIRELESS COMMUNICATIONS LETTERS, VOL. 15, 2026" / "3731".

rcs_anchor_candidates.name: 3GPP RAN1 agreed small-UAV RCS
rcs_anchor_candidates.why_it_matters: ⭐ A multi-company industry-consensus value, so it is cross-lab by construction - the single best antidote to sigma_anchor.py resting on one platform from one lab.
rcs_anchor_candidates.verbatim_quote: For UAV characterization, the agreed parameters comprise A = -12.81 dBsm, B1 = 0 dB, and B2 = 3.74 dB.

independent_corroboration.quote: The ST RCS is set to sigma_M = -12.81 Decibels relative to a square meter (dBsm), reflecting values proposed in ongoing 3GPP standardization efforts for small UAVs.

statistic_definition_is_stated.quote: The mean RCS in linear scale is given by E[X] = e^{mu+sigma^2/2}, with corresponding dBsm value A = 10 log10(E[X]) = 10 log10(e^{mu+sigma^2/2}).
statistic_definition_is_stated.why: ⭐ This makes A the dB of the LINEAR-domain mean - the same statistic family the ledger says Das uses (linear azimuth average). That is a genuine apples-to-apples handle for H2/H5.

caveats: The 3GPP value itself is not frequency-resolved in this quotation (B1 = 0 means no angle dependence is modelled for small UAVs).
I did NOT locate the primary 3GPP RAN1 document; both sources are secondary citations of it. Treat as CONSENSUS-REPORTED, not primary.

rcs_anchor_candidates.name: NYU Abu Dhabi measured small/mid UAV RCS (Azim, Bazzi, Bomfin, Chafii; Rappaport on the companion)
rcs_anchor_candidates.value: Small-Sized UAV A = -13.57 dBsm, B2 = 3.065 dB; Mid-Sized UAV A = -9.6 dBsm, B2 = 10.66 dB
rcs_anchor_candidates.why_it_matters: ⭐ A genuinely DIFFERENT LAB from Das (Oulu) and from Yuan (Southeast Univ). Measured, not modelled.
rcs_anchor_candidates.verbatim_quote: The derived log-normal parameters for small-sized UAVs yield A = -13.57 dBsm and B2 = 3.065 dB, demonstrating close agreement with 3GPP’s standardized values of A = -12.81 dBsm and B2 = 3.74 dB established through industry consensus.
rcs_anchor_candidates.measurement_conditions: 25-28 GHz, 1 GHz steps, H-H polarization, LoS, Sivers EVK02004 RFIC + USRP B205mini, 20 MHz bandwidth, Zadoff-Chu signalling, Tx-Rx height 1 m, NYU Abu Dhabi. The word "anechoic" does NOT appear - this is an indoor-factory-like environment.

companion.platforms: DJI Mavic 2 Pro and DJI Matrice 300 RTK, measured in flight while rotating, quasi-monostatic plus bistatic angles theta_b approx 10/20/40/60 deg, 25-28 GHz
companion.raw_fit_example: Mavic 2 Pro, 25 GHz, theta_b approx 10 deg, lognormal fit: mu = -3.9, sigma = 1.4 (KS 8.8e-2, MSE 2.3e-3)
companion.note: This companion paper reports NO dBsm values at all - only lognormal mu/sigma in the linear m^2 domain. Converting to dBsm is OUR derivation, not theirs.

caveats: ⚠ Band is 25-28 GHz. Our operating band is 2.4-5 GHz. This is NOT apples-to-apples on frequency.
⚠ 2505.08754 and 2502.11540 are the same group - they corroborate each other but count as ONE independent lab.

rcs_anchor_candidates.name: Yuan et al. anechoic-chamber monostatic UAV RCS, 1.8-18.2 GHz
rcs_anchor_candidates.value: Distribution fits (Rician best), parameters in the paper; slopes at theta = 90/0/180 deg per our ledger
rcs_anchor_candidates.why_it_matters: ⭐ Covers 1.8-18.2 GHz, i.e. it SPANS our 2.4/3.5/5 GHz band, and it is a different lab (Southeast University, Nanjing) from Das (Oulu).
rcs_anchor_candidates.source_status: venue UNVERIFIED (see H5) - the journal twin is IEEE AWPL 24:222-226, Jan 2025, DOI 10.1109/lawp.2024.3492502
caveats: ⚠ TWO Yuan documents exist (see H5). Do not blend them.

⚠ Lab-independence from Das is only PARTIAL: the AWPL twin is indexed as a 6G Flagship (Univ. Oulu) publication, so an Oulu co-affiliation is likely on at least one author. The conference PDF lists Southeast University only.

rcs_anchor_candidates.name: Das et al. multiband mono+bistatic AAV RCS
rcs_anchor_candidates.why_it_matters: Reconfirmed venue/pages/band (see H2). Its band 1.8-27 GHz contains our band.
caveats: ⚠ IEEE lists a supplementary file (DOI suffix /mm1) that we do NOT have.

rcs_anchor_candidates.name: Fenollosa et al. - evidence AGAINST simple frequency scaling
rcs_anchor_candidates.value: no drone measured; targets are an AGV, a pedestrian and a full-scale car
rcs_anchor_candidates.why_it_matters: ⭐ Directly undercuts the habit of extrapolating a single dB-per-GHz slope. Published (IEEE GLOBECOM Workshops 2024, DOI 10.1109/GCWkshp64532.2024.11101050).
rcs_anchor_candidates.verbatim_quote: Key findings highlight how much scaling RCS values based on frequency and geometry is complex and varies among different types of materials and shapes.
rcs_anchor_candidates.second_quote: However, the differences are not comparable to the scaling effects seen in simpler metallic objects like a metal plate or a metal cylinder, whose scalings for the studied frequencies would be approximately 7 dB and 3.5 dB, respectively.
rcs_anchor_candidates.measurement_conditions: VNA (R&S ZNB40), PEC-sphere calibration, background subtraction + time-domain gating, bands 10-15 GHz and 25.75-30.25 GHz, anechoic chamber 4.96 x 8.33 x 6.1 m "designed for up to 10 GHz use" with auxiliary absorbers to 40 GHz.
caveats: No drone. Use it as a methodological caution, never as a drone anchor.

unretrieved_leads.verbatim_abstract_fragment: The Monostatic-Bistatic Equivalence Theorem (MBET) and its variants are often used to estimate bistatic RCS, but their validity remains uncertain for complex targets and wide frequency bands. negative_findings: ⭐ Measured drone RCS at sub-6 GHz is genuinely scarce. Across every search surface, the drone-RCS literature clusters at 15-40 GHz. The only measurement sets found that reach our 2.4-5 GHz band are Das (1.8-27 GHz, published WCL) and Yuan (1.8-18.2 GHz, venue unverified) - and the L-band half of the LSS-FMCWR-1.0 dataset, which we do not have.
No Sionna fork or extension computing drone RCS was found. The only Sionna scattering extension located is Ziganshin (curved bodies, vehicular/ISAC, not drones).
Sagitta (2604.09243) is NOT a Sionna extension and NOT a drone paper: full-text census gives sionna=0 and drone/UAV=0.
No paper was found that does passive bistatic drone detection with a mesh-derived target signature - i.e. nothing occupying our exact cell.
